(3) <u>Comment</u>: Coddination between flood projects to prevent actions that would adversly affect flood heads and flood velocities at other points on the river.
Response: HUD is naturally interested in preventing a situation which would endanger other communities along the river. Approving a project that would, as part of its activity, encroach on the rivers in a way that would increase flood heads and flow velocities for communities other than the project area is not HUD's desire. This possibility is blocked by Pennsylvania State Law which requires that a permit be obtained through DER for any activity which would lead to an encroachment on the river, i.e., construction of levees, dykes same as land fill operations. All Federal agencies are also subject to and adhere to this state requirement. In addition, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers conduct public hearings on all of its projects during the planning stage. However, DER has the lead responsibility in coordinating these projects.
HUD's basic aid to the community involves grants to carry out certain specified activities which may involve actions that could change the character of the river. It does not directly carry out the activity. The entire program is administered by the locality and, therefore, subject to state laws regarding such activity. In addition the proposed Flood Plain Ordinance contains language that would prevent activities in the Plain which could increase the water surface elevation of the 100 year flood more than 1 foot in the area. It is reasonable to assume that levels at points above and below the locality will likewise not be increased to any measurable degree.
